text:
nina: quick check — repro from a customer shows the Go client (http2) leaves connections in USE_AFTER_CANCEL state and our retry middleware doesn't retry. seen this after context cancel in streaming path. anyone have a checklist for transport flags we should try?

max: can you paste the minimal transport config you were using?

nina: here is what i started with:
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  DisableKeepAlives: false,
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
  ExpectContinueTimeout: 1 * time.Second,
  DialContext: (&net.Dialer{Timeout: 30 * time.Second, KeepAlive: 30 * time.Second}).DialContext,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr, Timeout: 0} // we rely on context for cancel
```

sophia: a couple quick things: 1) are you using http2 Transport wrapper or relying on net/http to auto-upgrade? 2) ensure you don't set Transport.DisableKeepAlives = true in any path; that prevents reuse which can mask leaks.

ryan: also check MaxIdleConnsPerHost << number of concurrent streams — if it's too low you'll see contention and unexpected connection churn. for streaming cancels we historically had to increase IdleConnTimeout and not set client.Timeout.

nina: i'm explicitly enabling golang.org/x/net/http2 by calling http2.ConfigureTransport(tr) so it's using http2 stacks. logs show stream reset code= CANCEL but connection not closed.

max: when cancel happens, do you see `RST_STREAM` vs `GOAWAY` in the server logs? RST_STREAM should free the stream but keep conn; GOAWAY will close. which are you seeing?

nina: mostly RST_STREAM, sometimes a GOAWAY after a short while. attaching a small log snippet: 
```
2026-03-16T12:02:11Z client: stream 42 canceled context
2026-03-16T12:02:11Z client: sent RST_STREAM 42
2026-03-16T12:02:12Z client: stream 43 start
2026-03-16T12:02:15Z client: stream 43 stuck waiting for conn
```

sophia: could be conn pool starvation. try raising MaxIdleConnsPerHost to 300 and MaxConnsPerHost (Go1.11+) to match expected concurrency. also ensure K/V cache usage doesn't grow without bounds.

ryan: another angle — our retry middleware inspects errors to decide whether to retry. If request context was canceled we treat as non-retriable. For streaming partial failures we should surface an error type that allows idempotent retries. maybe add a small wrapper that converts some canceled streaming errors into retryable net errors with Temporary()=true.

nina: good point. i added an experiment to do that locally and got one more successful retry, but still observed a connection stuck in CLOSE_WAIT-ish state.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: i bumped the client-default MaxIdleConnsPerHost to 256 in staging at 2026-03-16T13:00Z for broader testing.

max: also check TCP keepalive intervals at the OS level. Our cloud VMs have a 2h default keepalive which is too long for transient cancellations. set net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time to 120s on staging if you can.

nina: will try the two axes: bump transports + OS keepalive + tweak retry classifier. i'll report back with simple perf numbers and leak counts. if this persists i'll open a tiny repro and @ryan can pair w/ me.

sophia: when you open the repro include: minimal client, server behavior (how it responds to RST_STREAM/GOAWAY), and pprof (goroutines + netstat) at the moment of stuck connections. that saved us last time.

nina: thanks — plan: run variations (MaxIdleConnsPerHost 100/256/512, MaxConnsPerHost same, IdleConnTimeout 30/90/180s, OS keepalive 120s), toggle retry classifier, collect pprof + netstat. will update this thread with results. :thumbsup:

ryan: sweet. if you want a quick helper script to run the matrix i can paste one in here.

nina: please do when you have a sec, that'd speed it up.

max: one last note — if you end up with long-lived connections that are idle, consider periodically issuing a lightweight `HEAD` probe through the same client to keep streams healthy rather than spinning up new conns.

nina: noted. thanks all, i'll post data in ~2h.
